A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TokSuite study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, allowing content to be matched across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of fourteen trained models, multilingual perturbation results, and decoding, model-scale and text-budget experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds initialization-seed experiments, training-loss curves and further external-model results.

M1.justification: The fourteen-tokenizer suite, vocabulary alignment, shared initialization and core training procedure are retained. V2 newly specifies untied embeddings, but does not establish an architectural change. Additional evaluation models and diagnostics do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: The five languages, training corpora, canonical questions and named evaluation benchmarks are retained. However, v1 Table 8's General subset, comprising 89 examples and four perturbation types, disappears from v2 Table 7. The PDFs do not explain whether distinct scenarios were removed or the inventory was corrected.

E2.justification: External comparisons are substantially revised: v2 adds Bolmo-1B/7B, c4ai-command-r-v01 and three additional Llama checkpoints, excludes external mBERT, and separates GPT-2 and Phi models into English-only comparisons. BLT and the larger Qwen models already appeared in v1. The fourteen controlled tokenizers and exact-byte comparison remain.

E3.justification: V2 restricts robustness evaluation of external GPT-2 and Phi models to English and introduces a normalized training-loss diagnostic in Appendix C.2. The core evaluation metric, training budgets and existing scale/text-matched settings remain unchanged; expanded descriptions do not establish reruns of those experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds training-convergence analysis through Figure 6 and initialization sensitivity through Appendix G.3. The scale, text-matched, exact-byte and detailed perturbation analyses already existed in v1 and are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Appendix G.3 explicitly adds two Llama-3.2-1B training runs using seeds 888 and 222 alongside the original seed 777, and compares variation with bootstrap intervals. The 10,000-trial bootstrap, 95% intervals and Wilcoxon testing already appeared in v1.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive canonical-accuracy reporting, seed results and external-model results, while retaining Table 1 and the controlled scale/text-matched robustness tables. External XGLM's reported average changes from 0.04 to 0.09. TokenMonster's canonical average changes from 0.759199 in v1 Table 5 to 0.80 in v2 Table 21, beyond rounding. These are reporting changes, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix C.2 introduces a mathematical specification for its new loss diagnostic, describing BPB as cross-entropy normalized by log2|V|. The vocabulary-unification definitions and initialization equations are unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the introduction's novelty claim about otherwise identical model collections to collections using off-the-shelf, industry-standard tokenizers. The central contributions—fourteen controlled models, a multilingual robustness benchmark and tokenizer-dependent robustness findings—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The new Discussion explicitly acknowledges entangled tokenizer properties, qualifies TokenMonster's robustness with lower canonical accuracy, and expands mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries. Appendix G.4 replaces v1's potentially favorable interpretation of external mBERT's negative degradation with a near-chance-baseline explanation and adds substantial qualifications concerning external and latent-byte models.

D1.justification: V2 adds eight-H100 hardware and three-to-five-day training estimates, training/configuration access instructions, an lm-eval command, and details of text-matched corpus reconstruction. Most core hyperparameters and data-access information were already present. V1's disclosure of Claude assistance in dataset development and writing is removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to dynamic token pooling, BLT, Bolmo and BPE-dropout, and more explicitly distinguishes its controls from Ali and Schmidt's earlier studies. Most cited work is retained; publication updates and moving Token Healing's reference into a footnote do not constitute new or removed research.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are substantially revised, Discussion and Impact Statement sections are added, and the appendices are reorganized with a contents list and separate decoding, ablation and statistical sections. Much of the methodological and case-study prose remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column conference layout. The original overview figure is split, intrinsic-metric panels become separate enlarged figures, and numerous displays are reformatted or relocated. V2 also adds the training-loss plot and canonical-accuracy and seed tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility, confound discussion and seed validation, but introduces material reporting problems. Its new Table 6 gives Gemma-2 Chinese/Italian accuracies of 0.97/0.82, conflicting with 0.78/0.98 in retained Table 21. The new BPB diagnostic also specifies vocabulary-size normalization without byte normalization. These issues affect baseline interpretation and the added training-comparability argument, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
